newsitem.title: USA: Automotive toolmaker's shares soar on buyback offer.
newsitem.headline: Automotive toolmaker's shares soar on buyback offer.

text.p: SPX Corp. stock soared nearly 14 percent Thursday, gaining $6.375 to $52.25 after the maker of automotive tools and parts said it would buy back about 18.4 percent of its stock for $48 to $56 per share.
The buyback, in the form of a Dutch auction starting Friday, will cover 2.7 million shares, Muskegon, Mich.-based SPX said.

"The company's purchase of its common stock in this way is an attractive and speedy use of financial resources that will result in a more efficient and balanced capital structure and a lower cost of capital," said SPX Chief Financial Officer Patrick O'Leary.

The company also said it took several other steps. They included: eliminating its quarterly dividend; completing a tender offer to repurchase certain debt instruments; receiving a firm commitment on a new $400-million credit line; and establishing a new internal debt-to-capital target ratio.
